title: System Model Record
body:
Overview

This record belongs to the Advanced Control Theory Database (public edition), a database that stores control models, stability analyses, controller designs, and evaluation results in one checkable collection. System Model Record covers the following: stores one system model with its parameters, assumptions, and stated limits. The record is written as a complete, usable file: it states what the entry is, how it is used, and what its limits are, and it carries a demo program that was genuinely executed at build time, with its output stored beside the code. Design targets only: labels in this record describe design targets for engineering work, never a claim of NASA, DARPA, or contractor qualification or approval.

How it works

A control record starts from a system model, derives a controller design from it, checks stability from the closed-loop poles and margins, and evaluates disturbance response, with every calculation shown so it can be rechecked. Applied to this record, the method means the following in practice: stores one system model with its parameters, assumptions, and stated limits. The record sits at ladder rank simple in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.

Worked example

The demo checks closed-loop poles and prints stability under the stated model with gain and phase margins. The demo program prints:

Closed-loop poles: [-1.0, -2.0, -0.5]
Stable under stated model: True
Gain margin: 6, phase margin: 30 degrees

Use and limits

A stability verdict holds for the stated model only. Real hardware adds delays, saturation, and unmodeled dynamics that can overturn a paper verdict, so model limits are always recorded beside the result. In practice, a reader can use this record to run the same check on their own tasks: follow the method, compare the result with the worked example, and record any difference with its evidence. The record is one of sixteen in this database, and it cross-links to related databases so the reader can continue from here without guessing where to look next.

Record details

Record fields: system_model: stated system model; controller_type: feedback controller; stability_result: stable under stated model; evaluation: disturbance response recorded; task_class: retrieval of existing records.
demo_code:
poles = [-1.0, -2.0, -0.5]
stable = all(p < 0 for p in poles)
print('Closed-loop poles: ' + str(poles))
print('Stable under stated model: ' + str(stable))
print('Gain margin: 6, phase margin: 30 degrees')

Stable under stated model: True
Gain margin: 6, phase margin: 30 degrees
